subject: CAIQ: telemetry sampling cadence & control harmonization for runtime logs
messages:
From: Liam Turner <liam.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ telemetry sampling question (runtime logs)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the CAIQ crosswalk you sent the other week. As we map the telemetry-related controls (mostly CCM-LOG-1 -> CCM-LOG-6 equivalents in our CSA matrix), we noticed some ambiguity around sampling expectations for runtime traces and ephemeral telemetry.

Two specific asks:
- What sampling cadence does Redwood use for log/trace evidence when customers request runtime samples for control validation? Do you provide continuous log exports, periodic snapshots, or ad-hoc extracts?
- Can you confirm which artifacts map directly to the CAIQ entries on telemetry collection, masking, and retention? A short pointer to the artifact names or a sample artifact would be very helpful.

If you can propose a recommended sampling plan (we generally prefer minimal collection but need reproducible evidence for auditors), that would accelerate our internal sign-off.

Appreciate it,
Liam Turner
Senior Compliance Manager
Acme Health
compliance@acmehealth.com

[attachment: audit_scope_request.pdf (pdf)]
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Liam Turner <liam.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ telemetry sampling question (runtime logs)

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear asks. I put together a short proposal and attached three artifacts for your review: a draft control harmonization spreadsheet, a telemetry extraction helper script (sh), and an internal evidence roster that lists owners and retention windows.

High level options for sampling cadence (pick one that fits your audit scope):
1) Periodic snapshot (recommended for routine audits):
   - Rolling 7-day snapshot captured quarterly (one 7-day window every quarter).
   - Provides representative traffic while minimizing footprint.
   - Artifacts: full log export (.ndjson), filtered trace set (.json), extraction manifest.

2) Event-triggered full pull (recommended for incident or high-risk controls):
   - Full extraction of the required windows on request (within 48 hours SLA).
   - Useful when auditors request specific intervals or incidents.

3) Continuous short-term export (only for customers who opt in):
   - 72-hour continuous export retained in customer-controlled bucket for 7 days.

Practical notes: our CAIQ mapping in the attached spreadsheet marks which artifacts map to CCM/CAIQ entries for masking, log integrity, and retention. For runtime traces specifically we map: CCM-LOG-3 (trace masking) -> trace-redaction-manifest.txt ; CCM-LOG-5 (retention) -> retention-policy-v2.pdf.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm which sampling cadence you prefer.
- Internal owners (Marissa/Jonas/Kimberly) validate the attachments and commit to the extraction turnaround times.

Attachments: caiq_control_harmonization_v1.xlsx; telemetry_extraction_script_v2.sh; evidence_ownership_roster.csv

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Compliance Enablement
Redwood Inference
